next_item_hypothesis: The demonstrated train-only behavior pattern is directed transition asymmetry: 314605 of 339519 directed pairs have no observed reverse event. This motivates, but does not establish, failure of flat item IDs. Hypothesis: flat content-only quantization can under-refine distinct directional successor branches sharing coarse semantic neighborhoods; negative curvature may retain shared coarse structure while separating finer branches. Stage2 builds item SIDs only; downstream T5 Stage3 ranks next items.

math_definition.architecture: Frozen content embedding maps to a 32-dimensional latent, quantized by three residual codebooks of 256 codes each; emit one global three-token SID per item.
math_definition.geometry_constants: Curved c=1.0; epsilon=0.00001; clamp arcosh argument to at least 1.0; shared fixed projection radius R=0.9. Flat arm uses c=0 in the same implementation. epsilon is used only to document the curvature-projection formula, not in the scored region.

operator.scored_distance: D_c^2(x,y)=d_c(x,y)^2=(1/c)*arcosh(1+2*c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2 for c>0; clamp the argument to max(argument,1.0). Stable arcosh uses log1p(u+sqrt(u*(u+2))) where u=z-1>=0.
operator.flat_limit: The squared distance tends exactly to 4*||x-y||^2; the unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||.
operator.c_dependent_rules_at_zero: At c=0 use D_0^2=4*||x-y||^2, the exact limit of the scored squared distance; the exponential map is the identity. The curvature projection radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at zero and is not applied; instead flat uses the same fixed projection ||x||<=R as curved. The objective uses squared distance in both arms.
operator.domain_policy: Every vector entering a distance in either arm is projected into the same closed ball ||x||<=R<1. Thus for c=1 all Poincare denominators are positive; curvature-dependent projection is outside the scored region.
operator.residual_operation_order: At each level: map content to initial latent (level one) or take prior residual; project that vector to radius R; assign nearest code by the arm's squared distance; project selected code to radius R; score projected code; subtract projected selected code from projected current residual; project resulting residual before the next assignment/distance. Project the sum reconstruction before scoring. This map -> project -> assign -> project-code -> score -> subtract -> project-residual order is identical in both arms.
operator.assignment_gradient: Hard argmin selects SID tokens only. Losses use an explicit straight-through estimator: forward uses hard projected selected codes; backward passes the derivative with respect to the continuous projected input through the hard assignment as identity, while selected code vectors receive their direct codebook-loss gradient. Projection uses its ordinary piecewise Jacobian. No loss relies on one-hot argmin gradients.

objective.anti_collapse: Content reconstruction L_rec is included with coefficient one in L_total. It reconstructs each frozen content latent from the three selected codes; identical codes for all items cannot in general reconstruct differing content latents. Its encoder gradient uses the declared straight-through path.

loss_equations.name: content_reconstruction
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: x:[N,32] projected content latent; q:[N,3,32] selected projected codes; I is the batch item index set.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: N=0 is invalid; do not evaluate.
loss_equations.target_circularity: x is frozen content-derived target; stop-gradient breaks parameter dependence.

loss_equations.name: commitment
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: r:[N,3,32] projected pre-assignment residuals; q:[N,3,32] selected projected codes.
loss_equations.normalization_and_reduction: Mean over items, levels, and dimensions.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: N=0 is invalid; do not evaluate.
loss_equations.target_circularity: Hard code target is stop-gradient; STE supplies input gradient.

loss_equations.name: codebook_reconstruction
loss_equations.normalization_and_reduction: Mean over items, levels, and dimensions.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: N=0 is invalid; do not evaluate.
loss_equations.target_circularity: Residual target is stop-gradient; selected codes receive direct gradient.

loss_equations.name: total_stage2_objective
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: Scalar component losses and existing frozen Stage2 coefficients beta_commit,beta_code.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: Invalid if any component has an empty batch.
loss_equations.target_circularity: All targets and gradient breaks are specified above; no parameter-dependent target cycle.

hyperbolic_necessity: Negative curvature is a testable inductive-bias hypothesis, not a conclusion from observed directionality or the literature. Nested shared neighborhoods with finer directional branches may suit negative curvature; inspected sources establish separate hyperbolic-sequence and generative-SID overlaps, not their combined efficacy. Stage2 metrics are leading diagnostics, while the behavioral claim is tested only downstream.
euclidean_control: Both arms use the same implementation, architecture, parameters, initialization, codebook initialization, optimizer, schedule, epochs, batch size, seeds, and budget. Only the scored squared-distance formula changes: curved D_c^2 versus its c->0 limit 4*||x-y||^2. Both retain the same fixed projection radius R. No graph arm or new training protocol.
effect_site: Code assignment, codebook geometry, and squared-distance reconstruction/commitment objective; no Stage2 ranking or user-conditioned prediction.
real_trigger_measurement: Train-only longest-prefix transition evidence motivates the hypothesis. Stage2 fitting may use frozen content embeddings and legal train-split item transitions only. Validation pairs are diagnostic only; test behavior is reserved for downstream Stage3.
training_only_inputs: Frozen content embeddings and train-split item transitions only. No validation/test behavior for fitting, future events, prediction-time user context, user bootstrap, or batch-composition signal.

protocol.sid_scope: one global three-token SID per item
protocol.stage3_role: downstream T5 ranks next items; Stage2 does not rank
protocol.training_configuration: inherit frozen Stage2 epochs, batch, schedule, seeds, optimizer, budget and codebook initialization verbatim

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_l1_hard_er
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Frozen validation has 52855 pairs, each one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] -> target. For each pair define hit by anchor first token equaling candidate first token; ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits, with negatives counted over the ten negatives. Compute per seed paired curved-minus-flat effect, then arithmetic mean over the enumerated seed set. Also report curved absolute ER against the frozen Resample admission reference (FROZEN_THRESHOLDS.valid_l1_hard_er); a zero negative-hit denominator is NULL.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Count distinct (k1,k2) over all items per arm and seed; paired effect is curved minus flat, aggregate by arithmetic mean over the enumerated seed set. Also compare curved absolute count with FROZEN_THRESHOLDS.level2_distinct_prefixes.

stage2_diagnostics.name: l3_refinement_gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Per arm/seed compute mean over items of log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|); paired effect is curved minus flat, aggregate by arithmetic mean over seeds.

stage2_diagnostics.name: l3_collision
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Per arm/seed compute share of items whose complete SID is shared with another item; paired effect is curved minus flat, aggregate by arithmetic mean over seeds.

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional_g3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: For each arm, seed and frozen validation pair (anchor a,target t), let (u,v,w) be the target SID, B_uv={items i:k1_i=u,k2_i=v}, n_l=|{i in B_uv:k3_i=l|, and n=|B_uv|. p_pref(l)=(n_l-1[l=w]+1)/(n-1+256), for l=0..255; this is positive even for unseen target third codes. Let C_a,l count train-only longest-prefix successor occurrences of anchor item a whose successor item has prefix (u,v) and third code l, and C_a=sum_l C_a,l. p_hist(l)=(C_a,l+p_pref(l))/(C_a+1). The target probability uses l=w in both distributions. Pair contribution is 0 if C_a=0, else log2(p_hist(w)/p_pref(w)); average contributions over the frozen validation pairs. Compute each seed's arm difference and arithmetic-mean aggregate over seeds. Alpha=1, K=256.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Use the frozen paired Stage3 seed set {42}; identical seed and all frozen settings in both arms. For each seed compute curved test_R@10 minus flat test_R@10. Aggregate as the arithmetic mean of those paired differences; report per-seed and aggregate values. Test events are never Stage2 inputs.

classification.falsified_if: For any registered metric, every per-seed value and its aggregate are defined and finite, and at least one is at or below its registered minimum_effect in its registered direction; or either absolute Stage2 admission metric fails its named FROZEN_THRESHOLDS comparison.
classification.passed_if: For every registered metric, every per-seed value and its aggregate are defined and finite and strictly exceeds its registered minimum_effect in its registered direction, and both absolute Stage2 admission comparisons pass.
classification.mixed_if: Otherwise, including conflicting outcomes or any NULL per-seed/aggregate value; any comparison involving a NULL seed is inconclusive, never passed or falsified.

falsifier.null_outcome_rule: If a seed-wise or aggregated change is undefined or non-finite (including zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum), classify that outcome NULL; any comparison involving any NULL seed is inconclusive rather than passed or falsified.
